options: It deletes the vehicle record if found
It looks up the vehicle by sys_id, and if none is found, responds with a 404 status and an error body instead of continuing
It always returns a 404, regardless of whether the vehicle exists
It queries the checkout table instead of the vehicle table
questions.explain: veh.get(vehicleId) returns false when no record matches that sys_id, so the script explicitly answers 404 and stops before trying to read fields off a record that doesn't exist.

questions.q: Why does the resource script use orderByDesc('sys_created_on') and setLimit(1) on the checkout query?
options: To delete all older checkout records for that vehicle
To sort vehicles alphabetically by make and model
To fetch only the single most recent checkout record for that vehicle
To guarantee the query returns zero results
questions.explain: Ordering descending by creation date and limiting to one row gets just the latest checkout record tied to that vehicle, which is what the status endpoint should report.

questions.q: What does the Business Rule in Part 2 actually do when a checkout's status changes to Returned?
options: It directly sets the vehicle's status to available in the same script
It calls the Scripted REST API defined in Part 1
It deletes the checkout record
It calls gs.eventQueue('vehicle.returned', current, ...) to announce the event, without updating the vehicle record itself
questions.explain: The Business Rule only raises the vehicle.returned event with gs.eventQueue() — it deliberately does not touch the vehicle record itself, leaving that to the Script Action.

options: They come from querying every record in the x_acme_fleet_vehicle table
They're hardcoded constants in the Script Action
They're read from request.pathParams, the same as the REST resource
They're the extra parameters the Business Rule passed into gs.eventQueue(), read here as event.parm1 and event.parm2
questions.explain: gs.eventQueue('vehicle.returned', current, current.vehicle.toString(), gs.getUserID()) passed those two string values, available in the listener as event.parm1 and event.parm2.

questions.q: What would it cost the team if the Business Rule updated the vehicle record directly instead of raising an event for a Script Action to handle?
options: Adding a second reaction to the same return (an email alert, an external sync) would require editing the Business Rule's own code instead of adding an independent listener
The REST resource in Part 1 would stop working entirely
Nothing — a Business Rule and a Script Action always produce identical coupling
GlideRecord updates would no longer be possible from a Business Rule
questions.explain: Raising an event keeps the trigger and its reactions decoupled — a new listener can be added without touching the code that detected the status change, which direct updates inside the Business Rule wouldn't allow.
